item.title: Surfing legend on riding the Oregon Coast's biggest waves
item.description: In this episode of the Explore Oregon Podcast , host Zach Urness and intern Riley Ellis talk about big wave surfing and the people who chase 25 to 50 foot waves off the Oregon Coast. Ellis interviews an Oregon surfing legend — Ollie Richardson. He's a Newport teacher, husband and father who also rides the state's largest waves. Because of his extensive big wave resume, dating back to the early 2000s, Richardson is a local legend on the Oregon Coast. Ellis, who grew up surfing in Lincoln City, remembers being a kid and watching Richardson tow-in to huge waves behind a jet ski. The two talk about the thrill of riding big waves, the potential dangers, and complexity of balancing regular life with such an extreme hobby. item.title: Liverpool have incredible new playmaker, he's better than Florian Wirtz
item.description: Liverpool have incredible new playmaker, he's better than Florian Wirtz Florian Wirtz is getting better at Liverpool but there's someone ready to takeover from him very soon. It's not quite been the esteem for the German midfielder that he expected when he first arrived at Anfield. Florian Wirtz came with a lot of promise but he hasn't really delivered those expectations. There have been great performances from the German. But they have also been juxtaposed by some utterly disappointing performances. On the balance of things, you'd have to say there have been more disappointing performances than great ones so far. That's a real shame because at one point in time while at Bayer Leverkusen it seemed like Wirtz was heading right to the very top of the game. He's young, and he still have time of course. How Liverpool can get the best out of Florian Wirtz For any playmaker in order for him to function well in a team, he needs to have the right teammates around him. It's impossible for a playmaker to do well if his teammates are not making the right runs. For a lot of his time at Liverpool Wirtz has had to balanced playing with a wide myriad of attackers. He's had to become accustomed to not just playing with one but multiple different types of players. That's a factor that will undoubtedly have an impact on his overall performance. There's also another element at play. A lot of the times, Liverpool cannot find Wirtz in the right areas. There's no coincidence that Wirtz plays better when Trey Nyoni and Jeremy Jacquet are both on the pitch. The duo are known for their ability to play line-breaking passes and are able to find Wirtz in better positions. Meet Liverpool's new incredible playmaker - AJ Yeguo Wirtz's problem is that he didn't grow up in England. He needs a lot more time to acclimatise to English football. That's something AJ Yeguo doesn't have to worry about. He has been at Liverpool's academy from a young age, and he has also represented both Poland and England's youth national teams. The young attacker, is only 17-years-old but he's catching the eye for the Reds' academy with his playmaking ability. He put on a great cameo for Liverpool's U19 side in the UEFA Youth League against LASK and impressed in the U18 Premier League where he has two goals and three assists in just six appearances. A quick and very physically strong player. Yeguo's creative flair combined with his physical qualities not only make him an incredible playmaker but it could make him better suited to the Premier League in comparison to Wirtz.

item.title: Oviedo golfer among 21-player field at Orlando APGA tournament
item.description: Oviedo resident Kamaiu Johnson is among 21 golfers competing this week in the Billy Horschel Invitational at Evermore Resort in Orlando. The Advocates Professional Golf Association Tour event runs Monday through Wednesday on Evermore Resort’s Cypress Course. Oviedo resident Kamaiu Johnson is among 21 golfers competing this week in the Billy Horschel Invitational at Evermore Resort in Orlando. The Advocates Professional Golf Association Tour event runs Monday through Wednesday on Evermore Resort’s Cypress Course. The field includes 19 APGA Tour professionals and two invited college golfers. Five players have won APGA events this year. Johnson, a Tallahassee native, has won eight APGA Tour titles. He has also made five PGA Tour starts, including appearances at the Arnold Palmer Invitational in 2021 and 2023. West Palm Beach resident Chase Johnson is also competing. He is a seven-time APGA Tour champion, won the organization’s Jeff Dailey Player of the Year award in 2023 and 2024 and most recently competed on the PGA Tour at the 2025 U.S. Open. Other players include 2026 APGA Tour event winners Xavier Bighaus, Andrew Fernandes, Kevin Hall, David Kim and Jonathan Yoshihiro. Tournament schedule The tournament began Monday with a pro-am and practice rounds. The first round begins at 10:20 a.m. Tuesday, followed by the final round at 10:10 a.m. Wednesday. The champion will receive $30,000 from the tournament’s $100,000 purse and 700 points toward the APGA’s Player of the Year standings. The event is the 13th of 15 tournaments on the APGA Tour’s 2026 schedule. The APGA was established in 2010 to expand opportunities in golf through professional tournaments, player development and mentoring programs. item.title: Packers rumors: Adam Schefter suggests Micah Parsons still weeks away from return
item.description: Tork Mason/Green Bay Press-Gazette Packers rumors: Adam Schefter suggests Micah Parsons still weeks away from return appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . At 4-2, the Green Bay Packers are tied with the Chicago Bears for second place in the NFC North. The duo are a game and a half behind the Minnesota Vikings at 5-0. Riding a three-game winning streak, the Packers will travel to Detroit to take on the Lions in a divisional clash. The Lions are right behind Green Bay at 3-2. They’ll also be fresh, coming off a bye week. While the Pack prepares for a pivotal matchup, they received an update on star edge rusher Micah Parsons . Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter on the Pat McAfee Show, Parsons is still at least a couple of weeks away from returning. McAfee shared Schefter’s report via X, formerly Twitter. “I was told that Micah Parsons wasn’t close to playing against the Dallas Cowboys,” Schefter said on the show. “They haven’t opened up his practice window yet, and I’m not anticipating that right now.” Schefter went on to state that Parsons likely wouldn’t be back until at least early next month. His knee injury has kept him on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list the entire season. While it would have been quite the storyline if Parsons returned this past Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys, his former team, his 21-day practice window still has not opened up. Before the ex-Cowboy can make his return, that window must open up. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) With a pivotal Sunday afternoon tilt against the Lions approaching, it sounds as if Parsons will continue his stint on the PUP. If Schefter’s timeline is correct, the earliest the Packers would get Parsons back could be in New England against the Patriots on November 8th. Green Bay’s bye is two weeks after that. It feels more likely that the former first-rounder will return against the Los Angeles Rams in a primetime matchup on Thanksgiving Eve. In any case, the sooner the Pack gets Parsons back, the better. Their postseason hopes may depend on it. They boast a 41.5% rushing success rate, five percentage points better than their first five games a season ago. That’s also good enough for sixth in the NFL. The Niners are also sixth in EPA per rush. Whether it’s on a down-to-down basis or limiting explosive plays, Raheem Morris’s scheme is getting the job done. Morris’s 5-down fronts take away the B-gap bubble and keep Fred Warner clean. When you take that out, how scary he is just running the ball. He’s got the speed and the coordination to win games only with his legs, which means you want to keep him in the pocket and not let him out because he can beat you with his legs. However, he’s a very scary quarterback in the pocket just playing the position. So, he’s got all the tools to be as good as there is.” Daniels is everything you want in a quarterback when you take him No. 1 overall. He’s unquestionably the most talented quarterback the Niners will have faced this season. Daniels has generated more EPA than Matthew Stafford despite playing 235 fewer snaps. McLaurin runs 77.3% of his routes on the outside and has caught only 53.8% of his targets. With the way Morris has structured his defense, the McLaurins of the world are rarely targeted. item.title: WPL 2027 Auction: 146 players, including 119 Indians, to go under the hammer for 27 slots in Kochi
item.description: The race to secure the remaining spots for the 2027 Women’s Premier League (WPL) season will intensify at the player auction in Kochi on October 28, with 146 cricketers set to go under the hammer for just 27 available slots across the five franchises. England batter Sophia Dunkley and Australia all-rounder Sophie Molineux headline the auction pool with the highest base price of Rs 50 lakh. According to a WPL press release, the auction list features 119 Indian players, including 22 capped and 97 uncapped cricketers, alongside 27 overseas players, comprising 14 capped and 13 uncapped names. Six overseas players represent Associate Nations. Of the 27 slots available, 20 are reserved for Indian players and seven for overseas recruits. The auction is scheduled to begin at 5:30 PM. Dunkley, Molineux lead highest base-price bracket Dunkley and Molineux have registered at the top base price of Rs 50 lakh, putting the England batter and Australia all-rounder among the headline names in the auction. India’s G Kamalini and Kiran Navgire, along with Australia’s Heather Graham and Jess Jonassen, have set their base price at Rs 40 lakh. Another 30 players have registered in the Rs 30 lakh bracket. With limited vacancies across the five franchises, teams will need to balance their remaining budgets and squad requirements while identifying players who can strengthen their line-ups ahead of the new season. Mumbai Indians acquire Tara Norris in trade Ahead of the auction, Mumbai Indians acquired USA left-arm seamer Tara Norris from UP Warriorz at her base price of Rs 10 lakh. Norris previously represented Delhi Capitals in the inaugural WPL season in 2023, making an immediate impact by becoming the first bowler in the tournament’s history to take a five-wicket haul. She returned figures of 5/29 against Royal Challengers Bengaluru at the Brabourne Stadium, dismissing Ellyse Perry, Heather Knight and Richa Ghosh among others. Her move to Mumbai adds another option to the franchise’s bowling resources ahead of the auction. With 146 players competing for 27 places, the Kochi auction will offer franchises a final opportunity to address gaps in their squads and build combinations for the 2027 WPL season.

item.title: Manchester United defenders “don’t feel welcome at the club”, won’t “play through injuries”
item.description: Manchester United defenders “don’t feel welcome at the club”, won’t “play through injuries” A number of Manchester United players are said to feel unwelcome at the club, with concerns that higher earners are being deliberately targeted to encourage their departure. Pay disputes and exit tensions precede fresh dressing-room claim On 10 March 2025, Sir Jim Ratcliffe described some United players as “not good enough” or “overpaid”. He named Casemiro, Rasmus Hojlund, Andre Onana, Antony and Jadon Sancho among the inherited commitments facing the club. Four days later, Bruno Fernandes responded that players did not want to be labelled overpaid and pointed out that the club had agreed the contracts in question. Further friction emerged in July 2025 when Marcus Rashford, Alejandro Garnacho, Antony, Sancho and Tyrell Malacia trained separately from the main group after United said all five wanted transfers. Fernandes then disclosed in April 2026 that United officials had told him they would not stand in his way if he accepted a major offer from Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal in 2025. More recently, Lisandro Martínez criticised the club’s summer recruitment after the 2-0 defeat at Atlético Madrid on 13 October 2026 and said he expected more from director of football Jason Wilcox. Sky Sports subsequently reported that Martínez had wanted to join Atlético during the summer, while at least one teammate challenged his public remarks. Multiple players allegedly feel pushed towards the exit Pilib De Brún (Phil Brown) from Beyond the Pitch on NBC Sports has now relayed an account from an individual whom he described as being in a position of knowledge about the situation at United. Brown claims the source told him: “A number of players don’t feel welcome at the club and feel that there is a deliberate targeting of higher paid players to get them to leave. “A number of the defenders wanted to leave this summer because they have been told they are being replaced in a year and some of those players are down to the last year of their contract. “Those players are not going to play through injuries for fear of jeopardizing a move and they feel that when they have played through injuries and had a poor game as a result, nobody ever explains to the fans that they have been carrying injuries. “Half that Utd team don’t want to be there because they feel like the club don’t want them to be there.” If Brown’s source is right, it could explain why it seems that Michael Carrick is working with one hand tied behind his back this season. and perhaps why the defence in particular has been so fragile. None of the older defenders have played well and there have been a number of injuries to the likes of Luke Shaw, Lisandro Martinez, Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt. Final Thoughts At the moment this is just hearsay, albeit from a club source to a reputable journalist. Nonetheless, it has a ring of truth to it and would explain a lot, including Martinez’ well-publicised outburst.

item.title: Cancelo, Gordon And Raphinha To Start | 4-2-3-1 Barcelona Predicted Lineup Vs Paris Saint-Germain
item.description: Cancelo, Gordon And Raphinha To Start | 4-2-3-1 Barcelona Predicted Lineup Vs Paris Saint-Germain Barcelona will face off against Paris Saint-Germain at Parc des Princes on Tuesday night as they look to secure a good result on the road in the UEFA Champions League. The Catalan club managed to earn a dominant 5-2 win away at Real Betis recently, which should keep them in good spirits going into this game. Hansi Flick will set his players up in a 4-2-3-1 formation and is expected to make a few changes to his first-team for this clash. Joao Cancelo, Anthony Gordon and Raphinha could all play from the start of this game. 4-2-3-1 Barcelona Predicted Lineup To Face Paris Saint-Germain Defence Joan Garcia will operate in between the sticks for Barcelona after conceding two goals in his last outing. Pau Cubarsi will resume his partnership with Gerard Martin at the heart of Flick’s defence as they focus on keeping a good shape on the defensive end of the field. Jules Kounde will try to impress as the right-back, while Joao Cancelo looks to prove his worth on the other side as the left-back. Both of them will get the license to go forward and express themselves inside the opponent’s half. Xavi Espart will be named on the bench as he provides cover for the left back position. SEVILLE, SPAIN – OCTOBER 17: Rodri of FC Barcelona celebrates scoring his team’s second goal during the LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 match between Real Betis Balompie and FC Barcelona at Estadio La Cartuja on October 17, 2026 in Seville, Spain. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) Midfield Rodri and Pedri will anchor the midfield for the Catalan giants as they look to make life difficult for the home team at the centre of the park and engineer some decent chances in the final third. The gifted trio of Anthony Gordon, Fermin Lopez and Lamine Yamal will operate just ahead of them as part of Flick’s attack. All three of them need to combine well if Barcelona are to come out on top in Paris this Tuesday night. Karim Adeyemi, Dani Olmo and Gavi will have to be content with a spot on the bench and might come on to influence the game in the second 45 minutes if required. Attack Raphinha will spearhead Barcelona’s attack up top. He has to figure out a way to be a real threat on the offensive end of the field. Gabriel Jesus will be available for selection on the bench as he waits for his chance to make an impact in the latter stages of the game if Barca are in need of a goal.

item.title: ‘Doesn’t Even Make Sense Anymore,’ ‘National Flag Football League’ — Buzz Patterson, Fans Rip Roughing the Passer After Lukas Van Ness Flag
item.description: Green Bay Packers defensive end Lukas Van Ness (90) reacts during the first quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Lambeau Field. (Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images) Buzz Patterson wants the NFL to fix roughing the passer. The former U.S. Air Force pilot said so early Monday, hours after a roughing call on Green Bay Packers defensive end Lukas Van Ness wiped out an interception in Green Bay’s 23-13 “Sunday Night Football” win over the Dallas Cowboys. The Packers led 23-7 in the fourth quarter at Lambeau Field when Carrington Valentine stepped in front of Jonathan Mingo and picked off Dak Prescott. Van Ness was flagged for roughing Prescott, the pick came off the board and the Cowboys kept the ball. Buzz Patterson Says the Rule No Longer Makes Sense Valentine’s pick would have been Green Bay’s third of the night, after Evan Williams and rookie Brandon Cisse intercepted Prescott in the second quarter. Valentine had come on for Cisse, who left in the second half with a shoulder stinger. “‘Roughing the passer’ doesn’t even make sense anymore. Fix this [NFL]! Ridiculous,” he wrote. One fan tied the post to Sunday night and to another Packers flag. “How was Van Ness gonna stop? Ridiculous call just like the taunting on Golden,” the fan wrote. That taunting flag came on Green Bay’s opening drive, when Matthew Golden beat DaRon Bland down the sideline for a 37-yard catch and was penalized afterward, leaving the ball at the Dallas 24. Golden capped the drive with a 9-yard touchdown catch from Jordan Love and finished with six catches for 104 yards. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: Pro Football Network’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Another fan argued the problem runs deeper than one call. “It is so arbitrary. I don’t see any clear rules for how to assess roughing. Hits that are essentially simultaneous to release of the ball — and showing replays in slow motion distorts what has happened — should never constitute a penalty.” Replays showed Van Ness pushing Prescott with two hands after the release, though the push didn’t appear to carry any real force, even if it knocked the Cowboys quarterback off his feet. Another fan argued the league has gone too far protecting quarterbacks. “Roughing would be driving him into the ground and breaking his ribs. Getting close to the National Flag Football League.” Another fan took that argument a step further. “Soon sacking the QB will be targeting.” Another fan, despite hating replay reviews, wants flags like this one looked at, calling them “game-changing plays.” And another fan has tuned out altogether, writing “I haven’t watched in years” and saying a move to Arizona gave them other things to do in the fall and winter. Lukas Van Ness Got Home Later on the Same Drive Dallas still didn’t cash in. Karl Brooks was flagged for roughing Prescott later on the same series before Van Ness sacked Prescott for a 3-yard loss. Prescott then threw his fourth-and-11 pass out of the back of the end zone, and the 14-play, 57-yard drive ended on downs.

item.title: VOTE for the HSS North Jersey Soccer Player of the Week for Oct. 12-18
item.description: After another wild week of the high school soccer season, it's time to look back on the best performances. Read about the players who stood out last week and let us know who you think should be the HSS North Jersey Player of the Week in the poll at the bottom of this page. Voting closes at 5 p.m. Thursday. Jason Baer, Tenafly senior goalkeeper Baer notched back-to-back shutouts in the Bergen County tournament and each one came with no room for error. He finished with 11 saves in a 1-0 win over Emerson and 14 stops when Tenafly beat Don Bosco 1-0 in the quarterfinals. Kyle Braithwaite, Bergen Catholic senior forward Braithwaite turned in quite a performance Saturday in the Bergen County quarterfinals, scoring all three Crusader goals in a 3-1 win over Northern Highlands. For the year, he leads Bergen Catholic with 18 goals. Michael DaSilva, Lakeland senior forward DaSilva sent Lakeland to its first Passaic County final since 1993 by picking up the lone goal in a 1-0 win over Clifton on Saturday. Earlier in the week, he chipped in two goals including the overtime winner in a 6-5 victory over DePaul. Danny Scuro, Demarest junior goalkeeper Scuro helped the 12 th -seeded Norsemen pull off two upsets and advance to their first county semifinal in at least two decades. He combined for 10 saves in shutout wins over Glen Rock and defending-champion Ramapo. Ellie Alvarado, Immaculate Heart sophomore goalkeeper Alvarado clinched back-to-back shutouts in her debut in the Bergen County tournament. She made nine saves against Northern Highlands and two against Pascack Valley. Hope Ernst, Ramsey junior forward The Virginia commit totaled four goals and three assists last week while pushing Ramsey back to the Bergen County semifinals. She reached 200 career points against Glen Rock on Oct. 13. item.title: Boston Celtics announce new partnership with Total Mortgage
item.description: The Boston Celtics announced a new partnership with Total Mortgage today via a press release circulated to the media, sharing the news that Total Mortgage will serve as the Official Mortgage Partner of the team for the coming 2026-27 NBA regular season. This collaboration unites two organizations that have strong ties to the greater New England region, a dedication to the communities that they serve, and a mutual goal of continually improving their standards. Total Mortgage and the Celtics are teaming up for the Home Assist campaign, which will run throughout the season, per the release. This initiative reportedly aims to showcase their dedication to promoting safe and affordable housing. For every assist made by the Celtics during the 2026-27 regular season, Total Mortgage will donate $18, honoring the franchise’s 18 championships. The donations will benefit Habitat for Humanity of Greater Boston, Inc., supporting its efforts to provide safe and affordable housing. "Total Mortgage has built a strong presence across New England and at the same time has maintained a clear commitment to the communities it serves," said Celtics Chief Partnership Officer Ted Dalton. "We see a real opportunity through this partnership to create meaningful programs for our fans and communities, including the Home Assist campaign, which will work towards supporting safe and affordable housing." "As one of the few mortgage companies in the country proudly headquartered in New England, we are thrilled to align the Total Mortgage brand with the Boston Celtics, one of the most storied and successful franchises in all of sports," said Total Mortgage, Chief Revenue Officer Christopher Affinito. "From the very first conversation with the Celtics, we recognized right away that our organizations shared the same common values in giving back to the local communities and markets we serve. This partnership marks a monumental moment for Total Mortgage, and we truly believe this move will play a vital role in our continued success and our growth here in New England." item.title: Craig Carton accuses ESPN of creating guide to encourage children to gamble

item.title: Brewers’ sweeping of Dodgers sets new NLCS viewership record not seen in 11 years
item.description: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Brewers’ sweeping of Dodgers sets new NLCS viewership record not seen in 11 years appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Dodgers will not win a third straight World Series. The Dodgers were eliminated from the MLB Playoffs after being swept by the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS. The Brewers will be heading to the World Series for the first time since 1982 . While the series went just four games, it set viewership records , per Fox Sports PR. “2026 NLCS on FOX & FS1 draws best average viewership for an LCS on any network since 2015,” Fox Sports PR posted on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) It was noted that 7.533 million viewrs turned in on average for the 2026 NLCS on Fox, FS1, and Fox Deportes. That was a 77 percent increase from the 2025 ALCS on Fox through four games. Over six million viewer turned in to NLCS Game 4 on FS1 and Fox Deportes, which was the most-watched LCS Game 4 on any network since 2018, and up 107 percent from Game 4 of the ALCS last year on Fox. MLB viewership numbers were up across the board this year. Fox saw their best increase since 2021, while NBC had a huge first year broadcasting MLB since the 2000 season. Still, there has to be some concern for Fox about the World Series. In the last two seasons, the World Series has averaged over 15 million viewers, but the Dodgers played in both series, while the New York Yankees played in 2024. Still, the 2023 World Series had the worst viewership numbers by average. That year, it was the Texas Rangers against the Arizona Diamondbacks. With the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays facing off in the ALCS, one of those two teams will be in the World Series. This means two small-market teams will be playing in the World Series, and that could impact viewership. Related: Chris Rose sounds off on MLB after Rays-Guardians rain delay fiasco

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo receives 30-day suspension and £215 fine for walking out on Portugal squad
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo receives 30-day suspension and £215 fine for walking out on Portugal squad The Portuguese Football Federation have punished Cristiano Ronaldo after the forward left the national team camp during the international break. The federation has fined Ronaldo a measly £215 and suspended him for 30 days. They released a statement that read : “It was decided to impose a 30-day suspension, in addition to a financial fine of 2.5 accounting units, equivalent to 255 euros (two hundred and fifty-five euros).” However, the federation did not specify which games the suspension would cover, or whether time already served would count towards the 30-day sanction. Ronaldo made headlines after suddenly leaving his country’s Nations League camp following a rift with manager Jorge Jesus. He later apologised for his behaviour , but accused Jesus of twice breaking his word to him. Per Ronaldo, the Portugal coach had agreed a plan under which he would miss the away fixtures against Norway and Denmark. However, on the morning of the Norway game, Jesus told him he would play for half an hour. Ronaldo kept warming up but was never brought off the bench. The former Real Madrid star was also unhappy that Jesus presented a completely different version of events to the media after agreeing to clarify things at his press conference. Ronaldo has earned 234 caps for Portugal, scoring 146 goals in the process. But he is a fading force, with his performances at the summer World Cup sparking massive criticism from fans.

item.title: Charley Hull demands one thing is outlawed from the professional game as she suggests rule change
item.description: Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images Love her or loathe her, it is impossible to argue that Charley Hull hasn’t done a lot for the women’s game since she burst onto the scene as a 16-year-old back in 2012. Hull, 30, has nine professional victories to her name, as well as five runner-up finishes in the major championships. She is honest as the day is long and never tries to be someone she isn’t. Whether you like Charley Hull or not, she definitely deserves respect for being completely authentic if nothing else. Hull regularly causes controversy by speaking her mind, and she has done exactly that once again by suggesting a new rule change to help combat slow play. Charley Hull wants slow play outlawed from the game Perhaps it should come as no surprise that one of Hull’s biggest pet peeves is slow play. The Englishwoman is one of the fastest players in the game, if not the fastest. When speaking to Golfweek , Hull responded when asked how she would fix the slow play problem that has infected the professional game. “Oh, God, I don’t know, “ Hull said. “ I think you should get banned from the tour for a year or a three-month ban to start off with, because I want to play golf and I’m sure the slow players want to play golf. “ If the punishment is strict enough, you’re not gonna play slower. You would make sure you’d play a lot quicker than we do. “ That would be quite an extreme measure, but perhaps golfing authorities need to start tackling the issue of slow play with more ruthlessness. Governing bodies must address slow play issue urgently There is absolutely no reason why professional golfers should take more than four hours and 30 minutes to play a round. Of course, slow play is not something that has only affected the women’s game. It is a problem that has plagued the men’s game as well. At Oakmont during the US Open last year, rounds were taking more than six hours to complete, and the same thing happened this year at Shinnecock Hills. The main problem for the game of golf in general is that young children watching the sport will quickly lose interest if rounds take so long. There is also the issue of men and women being out of the house for too long unless something changes very quickly. The professionals need to set the standards for the amateurs to follow. And Charley Hull’s suggestion that suspensions should be dished out for slow play may well be the only solution that actually helps tackle slow play.

item.title: Carlos Alcaraz now must win the Paris Masters to join Novak Djokovic and Rafael Nadal on exclusive list
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz will be desperate to win the Paris Masters this year for a plethora of reasons. After all, he will be the event’s second seed, and with Jannik Sinner having ended his season , what would have been the overwhelming favourite is no longer playing. This leaves just a handful of names capable of challenging him, although this part of the season has historically provided more shocks for the Spaniard than others. Just last week, his defeat at the hands of Zizou Bergs stunned the tennis world. Last year, Cam Norrie was a shock victor over Carlos Alcaraz in Paris. It can happen to the seven-time major champion. However, if he ever needed more incentive to win this final Masters 1000 event of the season, it’s the little slice of history that is on the line which should give him that boost. Carlos Alcaraz is chasing history with Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic After his defeat at the Shanghai Masters, there is just one Masters 1000 tournament left of the season. Having only managed to feature at Indian Wells, Miami and Monte Carlo before his injury, this represents just the fifth appearance Alcaraz has managed this season. But, it is his last opportunity to ensure that he does not go trophyless at this level during 2026, having actually won at least one Masters 1000 event every year for four straight seasons now. If he were to fail in Paris, that counter would reset in 2027, which would be particularly heartbreaking given he is so close to becoming the only other male player alongside Novak Djokovic and Rafael Nadal to have done so across five years. The Serbian has actually had two separate spells of six years, with Nadal’s ten-year stint between 2005 and 2014 holding the record by some distance. Alcaraz currently sits on four with the likes of Andre Agassi, Pete Sampras, Andy Murray and Roger Federer. Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images Interestingly, so does Sinner, with 2026 marking his fourth consecutive year. He will therefore have a chance to join this exclusive list next year, and overtake Alcaraz should he fail to win the Paris Masters. The 23-year-old has never won this event before, with a run to the quarter-finals marking his best-ever in 2022.

item.title: How bad is Marshawn Lloyd, historically speaking?
item.description: GREEN BAY, WI - OCTOBER 11: Green Bay Packers running back Marshawn Lloyd (32) scores a touchdown during a game between the Green Bay Packers and the Chicago Bears on October 11, 2026 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, WI. (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Marshawn Lloyd is a PROBLEM (derogatory). While the early woes of the Green Bay Packers’ offensive line have prevented any running back from really getting going, Kaleb Johnson at least averages 3.7 yards per carry , and Chris Brooks, prior to his injury, hit a solid 4.7 yards per carry. Now, those numbers are bolstered by a few long runs, and they have both been bad on a per play basis, but at least they’re bolstered by something . Marshawn Lloyd has no juice. If there was some sort of vampire plant that sucked all the juice out of useful plants, that is what he would be. He has anti-juice. He’s just pulp. How bad is it? Since the merger, there are only seven running backs ever to average 2.5 yards or less per carry for their career while having over 50 carries . Four of those backs ran in 1982 or earlier (Willie Spencer, Reece Morrison, Odell Lawson, and Michael Morton). Marshawn Lloyd, along with Keaontay Ingram and Isaiah Spiller) is one of only three to pull this off since 1982. It gets worse! The NFL’s wonderful NextGenStats site tracks how many yards a running back should have gotten each carry based on the blocking, quality of defense, and several other factors. Marshawn Lloyd is dead last in Rushing Yards Over Expected per Attempt (RYOE/ATT) with -1.55 . Yes, on average, every single carry he has gained 1.5 fewer yards than an average back who simply followed his blocking and then fell down. Alvin Kamara is second worst in this category with -1.19, which is WAY better than Lloyd. Lloyd also unsurprisingly “leads” the league in negative total Rushing Yards Over Expected (RYOE) with -75 , just edging JK Dobbins (-72). Lloyd has gained more yards than expected on just 27.1% of his total carries, or 13 of his total carries. And he’s doing all of this against light boxes, as only five running backs have faced light boxes less than Lloyd in the 2026 season. NextGenStats also tracks a metric simply called “Efficiency.” Efficiency tracks how many yards a back travels per yard gained. A lower efficiency metric indicates a more “North-South” runner. Marshawn Lloyd averaged 6.06 yards run per yard gained, the second least efficient total in football (Keaton Mitchell somehow averages 6.27). This is indicative of Lloyd’s tendency to bounce runs outside even when putting his head down and charging forward is clearly the best idea. While the passing game is more important than the running game in football, you cannot survive with this level of play for very long. item.title: Luciano Spalletti set to continue at Juventus despite Lazio disaster
item.description: Luciano Spalletti set to continue at Juventus despite Lazio disaster Serie A side Juventus took a heavy 3-0 loss to Lazio on Sunday and Luciano Spalletti’s future has come into question from a lot of corners. item.title: Banana Ball returns to Texas in 2027: Dates, tickets
item.description: Banana Ball, known for its fast-paced rules and lively atmosphere, will return to El Paso in 2027 with the Texas Tailgaters playing the Party Animals. The El Paso dates will be June 18-19 at Southwest University Park. The Party Animals debuted in 2020 as rivals to the Savannah Bananas and have since become a fan favorite on the Banana Ball World Tour. The Texas Tailgaters joined the Banana Ball Championship League (BBCL) in 2025 and recently claimed the inaugural Banana Bowl championship. The Banana Ball YouTube channel announced the 2027 schedule on Thursday, Oct. 15. For 2027, the world tour will add two countries — Canada and Mexico. This year, El Pasoans got a taste of Banana Ball when the Texas Tailgaters swept their two-game series against the Firefighters in May at Southwest University Park. Both games were sold-out events. Banana Ball Lottery 2027 Fans interested in purchasing tickets are encouraged to sign up for the lottery . The official 2027 ticket lottery is open through Oct. 31. Note that entering doesn't guarantee a chance to purchase tickets. item.title: 📸 James Maddison ends 610-day wait with stunning Tottenham strike
item.description: 📸 James Maddison ends 610-day wait with stunning Tottenham strike I guess you could say this was exactly what the doctor ordered for Tottenham. Finally, the wait is over and they've scored first in a Premier League fixture for the first time this season. It is also somewhat poetic that it has come from the right foot of James Maddison, who starts a Premier League game tonight for the first time since April 2025. The midfielder has experienced cruel luck with injuries, including a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament that kept him sidelined for nine months. Just shy of the 15-minute mark against Coventry City, Mohammed Kudus laid it back to Maddison on the edge of the box and he curled a beautiful effort into the top corner to score against his former club. It's Maddison's first Premier League goal since February 2025, with his last one coming against Manchester United in a narrow 1-0 win. Can Spurs finally go on to win their first Premier League game of the season, or will Coventry be able to mount a comeback?

item.description: Leicester City won the FA Cup just five years ago but have since dropped down to League One [Shutterstock] Leicester City will travel to National League North side Oxford City in the 2026-27 FA Cup first round. It is the first time the Foxes have taken part at this stage of the competition since 2008 and they face sixth-tier opposition for a place in the second round. The 2021 winners were relegated to League One for this season with Russell Martin's side currently 14th having had an inconsistent start to the season. Meanwhile, there will be a family affair as Peterborough United face Reading as Posh boss Robbie Savage will take on his son Charlie's side when the first round kicks off around the weekend of Saturday, 7 November. A whopping 91 teams were named during the draw with four sides reaching the first round proper for the first time. Lowest-ranked team Tadley Calleva came from behind twice to force a replay with Aldershot and will make the trip to League One Barnsley should they progress. Meanwhile highest-ranked team Bradford City will welcome National League North side Marine as the League One leaders enter the competition. Eighth-tier AFC Rushden & Diamonds have won five games in the competition this season to reach the first round, with their reward a trip to League One side Burton Albion. item.title: Chelsea's Emiliano Martínez confirms return timeline after successful surgery on fractured jaw
item.description: Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez suffered a fractured jaw against Everton -Credit:Instagram Emiliano Martínez has confirmed he will be "back in a few weeks" after undergoing surgery following a horrific head collision during Chelsea's 2-0 win at Everton. Martínez collided heads with Jarrad Branthwaite as both players challenged for a cross, and following more than eight minutes of treatment on the field, the Argentina international was carried off on a stretcher into an awaiting ambulance. The goalkeeper subsequently posted a picture of himself in a hospital bed on Instagram, stating via football.london : "Thanks to everyone for the messages, the operation went well. The most important thing is that we won and with a clean sheet. We'll be back in a few weeks." Cristiano Ronaldo delivers brutal Portugal 'ultimatum' after Jorge Jesus 'broke his word' Manchester United stars claim interview ban after Lisandro Martínez outburst -Credit:NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images Martínez's club colleagues demonstrated their solidarity with the injured netminder, with Moises Caicedo and Morgan Rogers among those responding to his social media update. Caicedo posted "my brother" while Rogers called Martínez "my goalkeeper". Chelsea subsequently issued a statement on Sunday verifying that the goalkeeper suffered a jaw fracture. It read: "Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has undergone successful surgery on a fractured jaw. "Martínez was injured following a collision midway through the second half of our 2-0 victory over Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE "Martínez was taken to hospital for further assessment, which confirmed a fractured jaw that required surgery. "Everyone at Chelsea wishes Emi a speedy recovery and will support him throughout." Before sustaining his injury, Martínez had contributed to Chelsea's 2-0 victory, which also earned his side their first Premier League clean sheet in nine months. Speaking shortly after the final whistle, Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso revealed that Martínez had been transported to hospital for "precautionary tests". With Martínez sidelined, it'll now be down to 21-year-old Mike Penders to fill in between the sticks for Chelsea, with their next game scheduled for Saturday when they host Tottenham Hotspur.

item.description: Bruised Bundesliga champions hit a supposed rival for six and their flying winger is peaking at a perfect moment When Bayern Munich fail to win for two games in a row, you know what is coming next. Particularly on a Saturday night showcase, against the sort of good domestic opposition that tend to bring the best out of the champions. It had been a frustrating week, domestically and continentally, in two games on the road. On both occasions they had been caught cold, conceding the Bundesliga’s fastest goal at Augsburg and going 1-0 down in less than 90 seconds in Stavanger . Vincent Kompany’s low profile on the Allianz Arena touchline, almost motionless in his seat as his team rattled a flurry of goals past poor RB Leipzig, had nothing to do with any lingering chagrin connected to those slow starts from his team. The sporting director, Max Eberl, who stood in for his coach in the post-match press conference, explained that the Belgian had been ill, not to mention Kompany’s current hip problem that had made the move from dressing room to pitchside slow and uncomfortable. item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: A famous name and record attendances have given FCK a platform but a difficult start in Denmark’s top-flight shows success on the pitch is not guaranteed On an August day in 2024, 5,165 fans gathered at Vanløse Idrætspark to watch FC Copenhagen (FCK) take on B73 Slagelse in their first league match. For Denmark’s most successful men’s club, with 16 league titles, it marked the realisation of their desire to establish a women’s team, through collaboration with the existing FC Damsø, and an ambitious project with aims of having a wide-reaching impact on and off the pitch. The 26 months since have brought a whirlwind of success, the club securing back-to-back promotions to reach the A-Liga. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina career turned football into a sacred mystery
item.description: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
